name: Nassereith
kurzbeschreibung: Market town at the entrance to the Gurgltal valley at 843 m, known for the Schellerlaufen and the Dormitz pilgrimage church.
beschreibung:
Nassereith is a market town in the district of Imst at around 843 m above sea level at the entrance to the Gurgltal valley, where the Roman road Via Claudia Augusta from the Fernpass to Imst and the old salt road over the Holzleitensattel once crossed. The municipality has around 2,200 inhabitants.

Culturally defining is the Nassereither Schellerlaufen, an ancient carnival custom that is part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage and takes place only every three years. The Fasnachtshaus (carnival house) is dedicated to it. Also worth seeing are the pilgrimage church of St. Nikolaus in Dormitz and the parish church of the Three Holy Kings with its onion dome over 300 years old. The local Nassereither See and the nearby Fernsteinsee invite you to hike and fish.
text:
Overview

Nassereith is situated at the southern foot of the historic Fern Pass at the entrance to the Gurgl Valley in the Tyrolean Oberland, within the Imst district, approximately twelve kilometers north of the district capital Imst at an altitude of 838 meters. Home to roughly 2,220 residents and covering 72.4 square kilometers, this historic market town nestles into a broad mountain basin framed by the rugged limestone cliffs of the Mieming Range with the 2,493-meter Wannig, the Lechtal Alps, and the Tschirgant massif. Nassereith is internationally renowned among rock climbers within the Climbers Paradise network and boasts the Nassereith Schellerlaufen, recognized as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. Crystal-clear spring-fed lakes, vibrant woodcarving traditions, and active community life make Nassereith a compelling destination for sport and relaxation.

History

Human settlement in Nassereith dates back to Roman antiquity, when the vital imperial highway Via Claudia Augusta traversed the Fern Pass through this territory. The hamlet of Dormitz was first documented around 1050–1150, while the cliff fortress of Klause Fernstein served as a fortified toll station from 1288 onwards. For centuries, Nassereith prospered from overland transit trade, packhorse logistics, and tavern hospitality at the junction leading down into the Inn Valley. Between the 15th and 19th centuries, lead mining also thrived on the slopes of the Dirstentritt. The grand parish church of the Epiphany (Heilige Drei Könige) was erected in 1846–1847 as a three-aisled historicist church with Neo-Romanesque features and a Baroque north tower. The high altarpiece was gifted by Empress Maria Anna of Austria. The cultural crown jewel is the ancient Schellerlaufen carnival, rooted in the 18th century to celebrate the triumph of spring over winter.

Getting There

Nassereith enjoys first-rate road connections along one of the primary trans-Alpine corridors. Motorists travel directly via the B179 Fernpassstraße coming from Germany (Füssen/Reutte), or via the A12 Inntal Autobahn exiting at Mötz across the Mieming Plateau (B189) or at Imst through the Gurgl Valley. Rail travelers arrive at Imst-Pitztal or Ötztal stations along the Arlberg Railway line. From both hubs as well as from Innsbruck and Telfs, frequent regional VVT buses (including route 160G) run directly to Nassereith village center, ensuring smooth, sustainable public transit.

Tips

The cultural pinnacle is the Nassereith Schellerlaufen carnival celebrated once every three years; in interim years, the local Fasnacht Museum showcases over 450 intricately carved wooden masks and an immersive multimedia experience of this UNESCO tradition. Right in the heart of town, the emerald Nassereither See resting beneath a sheer cliff face invites visitors for leisurely lakeside strolls and refreshments. Rock climbers flock to the Sparchet climbing garden, featuring more than 100 well-bolted limestone pitches for all skill levels, alongside the challenging Leite via ferrata. Hikers will enjoy summiting the Hochwannig or walking the family-friendly Rossbachtal trail to the Adlerhorst panoramic viewpoint.
